source_evidence_candidates.exact_quote:
The manuscript presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a fast-track training
programme developed within the Horizon 2020 VITALISE project, aimed at enhancing researchers’
competencies in Living Lab methodologies. The topic is relevant and timely, particularly in the
context of European research infrastructures, user-centred innovation, and Responsible Research
and Innovation (RRI).

research outcomes to market implementation (Fauth et al., 2024;
Leminen & Westerlund, 2016). Living Labs can be defined
as open innovation ecosystems in real-life operational environments which put citizens and/or end-users at the centre of the
innovation process (European Network of Living Labs, 2025).
They promote a systematic user co-creation approach that
integrates research and innovation activities in communities and/or multi-stakeholder environments. Beyond their role
as co-creation environments, Living Labs act as orchestrators
within regional innovation ecosystems, facilitating collaboration across stakeholders and aligning innovation activities with
societal challenges (Fauth et al., 2024). These ecosystems reflect
the principles of the Quadruple Helix innovation model, where
